docs.title: vexy-stax
docs.text:
vexy-stax renders a deck of layered PNG slides as 3D glass plates. You describe the deck once, in a JSON scene file, and vexy-stax produces:

  • an expanded still: an angled hero shot with the plates spaced apart and captions visible,
  • a compact still: a head-on stack with the plates collapsed into one composite image,
  • a transition video that morphs between the two views.

This site documents vexy-stax-py, the offline Python package. It is published on PyPI as vexy-stax and installs the vexy-stax command. A browser sibling, vexy-stax-js, reads the same scene format and renders it with three.js.

docs.title: What goes in, what comes out
docs.text:
Input is a folder of layered images (for example, the layers you export from a design tool) and a scene file that lists them back to front:

{
  "version": 1,
  "slides": [
    { "src": "layer-0-background.png" },
    { "src": "layer-1-content.png" },
    { "src": "layer-2-ui.png" }
  ]
}

Every other scene field has a default. From that file the vexy-stax command renders:

vexy-stax render scene.json --view expanded --out beauty.png   # angled hero shot
vexy-stax render scene.json --view compact  --out stack.png    # head-on stack
vexy-stax video  scene.json --out morph.mp4                    # needs a "transition" block
vexy-stax overlay scene.json --out flat.png                    # flat 2D composite, no 3D engine

You don't have to write the scene by hand: vexy-stax dir2scene assets/ scans a folder and writes one for you.

docs.title: Three engines, one geometry
docs.text:
vexy-stax-py draws with one of three interchangeable engines:

Engine How it draws Default for pygfx Off-screen GPU rendering with pygfx/WGPU stills (render) blender Runs Blender in the background with Cycles (or Eevee in turbo mode) video (video) playwright Loads the built vexy-stax-js bundle in headless Chromium —

All three take their camera poses, plate spacing and opacities from one module, vexy_stax.geometry. The engines differ only in how they draw, so the same scene frames the same way in every engine.

docs.title: Live demos
docs.text:
The browser renderer runs these demos:

  • Animated demo: play the compact-to-expanded transition, or toggle the two views by hand.
  • Scrollspy demo: the deck rises into view and unfolds as you scroll.

docs.title: Design principles
docs.text:
Parse, don't validate. The scene is parsed once, at the boundary, into Pydantic models with extra="forbid". If load_scene() returns, the scene is valid; the rest of the code does not re-check fields.

Shared math, separate drawing. geometry.py holds every formula for camera placement, spacing, opacity and caption layout. Engines only draw the poses and per-frame values it produces. vexy-stax-js mirrors the same module in geometry.js, so a geometry change must land in both.

Cheap engine discovery. engines/base.py probes engines without importing them (shutil.which, importlib.util.find_spec) and imports the engine modules only when the registry is first used.

Fail loudly. Unknown scene fields, unknown engines, missing transitions, a missing ffmpeg or a missing JS bundle all raise errors that name the cause and, where possible, the fix.

docs.title: Changing the geometry
docs.text:
Geometry changes affect every renderer. Work in this order:

  1. Update SPEC.md section 3, which is the source of truth.
  2. Change src/vexy_stax/geometry.py and vexy-stax-js/src/geometry.js together.
  3. Update the expectations in tests/test_geometry.py and the JS tests.
  4. Run python example.py to render the showcase with every available engine, then uv run -s verify_302.py to compare the engines' output.

docs.title: Changing the scene format
docs.text: The format is versioned ("version": 1). Adding an optional field with a default that keeps the old behaviour is backward compatible. Update scene.py, the JSON Schema in schema/, and the JS parser together. Removing a field or changing its meaning needs a version bump.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
uv run pytest -q                 # default selection: everything except "slow"
uv run pytest -q -m slow         # long video renders
uv run pytest -q -m blender      # only the Blender tests
File Covers tests/test_scene.py model parsing, defaults, rejection of unknown fields, load_scene() tests/test_geometry.py cameras, gaps, frame plans, captions, easing, opacity tests/test_cli.py dir2scene output, sorting, flags, captions, errors tests/test_images.py Pillow overlay tests/test_juicy.py colour correction tests/test_pygfx.py, tests/test_blender.py, tests/test_playwright.py engine renders

The markers blender, pygfx, playwright and slow are declared in pyproject.toml. Engine tests skip themselves when the engine is unavailable. Tests use the sample deck in testdata/airbl-lores/ (nine layers, 1247 × 806), so they run without network access.

docs.title: Code style
docs.text:
• Ruff for linting and formatting (line-length = 120, target Python 3.12, rules E, F, I, UP).
  • Type hints throughout; mypy is configured in pyproject.toml. _blender_render.py is excluded because it imports bpy, which only exists inside Blender.
  • Every source file carries a this_file: comment with its path.

docs.title: Building
docs.text:
./build.sh in the repository root builds everything:

./build.sh            # lint + tests, docs, package
./build.sh test       # ruff check --fix, ruff format, pytest
./build.sh docs       # src_docs/build.sh → docs/
./build.sh package    # uv build into dist/, then twine check

The documentation alone can be built or previewed with:

src_docs/build.sh          # strict build into docs/
src_docs/build.sh serve    # live preview on http://127.0.0.1:8000

docs.title: Versions and releases
docs.text:
The version comes from git tags through hatch-vcs ([tool.hatch.version] source = "vcs"), which writes src/vexy_stax/_version.py at build time. That file is ignored by git.

./publish.sh makes a release:

  1. uvx gitnextver commits pending changes, tags the next vX.Y.Z and pushes.
  2. The script checks that HEAD carries a vX.Y.Z tag and stops if not.
  3. ./build.sh package builds the sdist and wheel and checks them with twine.
  4. uv publish uploads them. It needs UV_PUBLISH_TOKEN or another uv publish credential.

Pushing the tag also starts the Release GitHub workflow, which builds the package and uploads it with PyPI trusted publishing (skip-existing, so a version already uploaded by publish.sh doesn't fail it) and creates a GitHub release with the built files.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text: The documentation sources are in src_docs/md/, configured by src_docs/mkdocs.yml. The Docs workflow rebuilds docs/ on every push to main that touches src_docs/, and GitHub Pages serves docs/ at https://vexy.dev/vexy-stax-py/. Edit the Markdown in src_docs/md/, never the generated HTML in docs/.

docs.title: vexy-stax-js
docs.text: vexy-stax-js is the browser counterpart of vexy-stax-py. It reads the same scene format and renders it live with three.js. Its own documentation covers the JavaScript API; this page explains how the two packages relate.

docs.title: What the two packages share
docs.text:
Shared piece Python JavaScript Scene format vexy_stax/scene.py (Pydantic) src/scene.js JSON Schema schema/vexy-stax-scene.schema.json the same schema View math vexy_stax/geometry.py src/geometry.js

Both parsers reject unknown fields, and both geometry modules implement the formulas in Geometry, including the bisection solve for the expanded camera. A scene file written for one package renders with the same framing in the other.

There are two deliberate differences:

  • juicy is a Python-only field; vexy-stax-js ignores it.
  • The live browser element passes its container's aspect ratio as viewport_aspect to the camera functions, so the deck fills a container whose shape differs from the scene. The offline Python engines render at scene.size and use the scene's own aspect ratio.

docs.title: What the browser package adds
docs.text:
vexy-stax-js ships as a <vexy-stax> Web Component, an ES module and a classic-script global. Beyond stills and video export it can play the transition interactively and drive it from page scrolling. See the live demos:

  • Animated demo
  • Scrollspy demo

docs.title: The Playwright engine uses the JS build
docs.text:
The playwright engine in vexy-stax-py does not draw the plates itself. It loads vexy-stax-js/dist/vexy-stax.element.js in headless Chromium, mounts the scene in a <vexy-stax> element and captures the canvas. For video it computes frame_plan() in Python and pushes each frame state into the page with stage.applyFrameState, so Python decides every frame and three.js draws it.

To use it, check out both repositories side by side and build the JS bundle:

github.vexyart/
├── vexy-stax-js/     # npm install && npm run build → dist/vexy-stax.element.js
└── vexy-stax-py/

cd vexy-stax-js
npm install
npm run build

Rendering the same scene with --engine playwright and with --engine pygfx or --engine blender is the quickest way to compare the browser output with the offline renderers.

docs.title: Captions
docs.text: A caption is a short text label for one slide. vexy-stax draws it as a small opaque caption plate with the text centred on it. Caption sizes, positions and opacities come from vexy_stax.geometry, so all engines place them the same way.

docs.title: Turning captions on and off
docs.text:
• Scene-wide: "captions": false removes every caption plate, and the slide plates stand directly on the floor. The default is true.
  • Per slide: omit caption, or set "show_in": "none".
  • When generating a scene: vexy-stax dir2scene assets --nocaptions.

docs.title: Layout
docs.text:
With captions on, each slide forms a two-part stack at its own depth:

  • the caption plate stands on the floor (its bottom edge on the floor line Y = −height/2), left-aligned with the slide plate;
  • the slide plate is lifted by one caption-plate height, so it sits on top of the caption plate.

Both keep the slide's Z position, so in the angled expanded view each caption recedes with its slide.

docs.title: Size
docs.text:
All sizes derive from the caption size, 1 em in scene points:

Quantity Formula 1920 × 1080 scene Caption size (caption_size) caption_defaults.size, else max(8, 0.10 × height) 108 Plate height (caption_plate_height) caption size / 0.75 144 Plate centre Y (caption_plate_center_y) −height/2 + plate height/2 −468 Text baseline Y (caption_baseline_y) −height/2 + 1.0 em −432 Left edge X (caption_anchor_x) −width/2 −960 Plate width text width + 0.75 em padding on each side depends on the text Slide lift (slide_lift) plate height 144

The text always takes 75 % of the plate height, whether the size is the default or set explicitly.

docs.title: Colours and border
docs.text:
Element Default Set with Text #222222 caption_defaults.color, or a caption's style.color Plate fill edge.color (#f2f2f2) caption_defaults.fill_color Plate border colour edge.color caption_defaults.border_color Border thickness edge.width × height (0, off) edge.width

The caption border uses the same thickness as the slide-plate border, so with the default edge.width of 0 neither has a border.

docs.title: Font
docs.text:
The default font is the bundled vexy-stax.ttf (Zalando Sans Expanded). vexy-stax-js matches it with the Google Font "Zalando Sans" at width 125 and weight 500.

To use another font, give a path to a font file:

"caption_defaults": { "font": "/Library/Fonts/MyFont.ttf" }

A file path works in all engines. The Blender engine replaces anything that isn't an existing file with the bundled font. pygfx registers font files on the fly, maps "vexy-stax", "vexy stax", "zalando sans" and "zalando sans expanded" to the bundled font, and passes other family names to its font manager.

docs.title: Visibility per view
docs.text: show_in Compact Expanded During a transition expanded (default) 0 1 Fades in near the expanded end, staggered compact 1 0 1 − t both 1 1 1 none 0 0 0

docs.title: Fade timing
docs.text:
caption_opacities(scene, t) returns one opacity per slide at morph factor t (0 = compact, 1 = expanded). Engines call it for every frame. For an expanded caption on slide i of N:

spread = stagger × window
start_i = (1 − window) + (i / (N − 1)) × spread
ramp    = window − spread
opacity = clamp((t − start_i) / ramp, 0, 1)

So the backmost caption starts first, at t = 1 − window, and the frontmost reaches full opacity exactly at t = 1. Captions are fully visible only in the expanded view.

With the defaults (window 0.9, stagger 0.3) and three slides, spread is 0.27 and ramp 0.63:

t Slide 0 Slide 1 Slide 2 0.1 0.000 0.000 0.000 0.5 0.635 0.421 0.206 0.75 1.000 0.817 0.603 0.9 1.000 1.000 0.841 1.0 1.000 1.000 1.000

docs.title: Stagger in frames
docs.text:
caption_fade.stagger_frames sets the step between consecutive captions in transition frames instead. It applies only when the scene has a transition. The step becomes stagger_frames / leg_frames of the morph, where leg_frames = round(duration × transition.fps), and the total spread is capped at 95 % of the window so the frontmost caption still finishes at t = 1.

"caption_fade": { "stagger_frames": 3 }

With duration 3.0 at 30 fps (90 frames per leg), each caption starts 3 frames (0.1 s) after the one behind it.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
{
  "version": 1,
  "caption_defaults": { "size": 108, "color": "#222222" },
  "caption_fade": { "window": 0.9, "stagger": 0.3 },
  "slides": [
    { "src": "layer-0-bg.png", "caption": { "text": "Background" } },
    {
      "src": "layer-1-content.png",
      "caption": { "text": "Content", "style": { "color": "#0066cc" } }
    },
    { "src": "layer-2-ui.png", "caption": { "text": "UI", "show_in": "both" } }
  ]
}

docs.title: CLI
docs.text:
The vexy-stax command is built with Fire and Rich. Every subcommand is a method of the Stax class in src/vexy_stax/cli.py. python -m vexy_stax runs the same CLI.

vexy-stax COMMAND [ARGS] [FLAGS]

  dir2scene   Generate a scene JSON from a directory of images
  render      Render one still in the expanded or compact view
  video       Render the scene's transition to a video file
  overlay     Flat Pillow composite of the slides, no 3D engine
  engines     List the engines whose dependencies are available

vexy-stax COMMAND --help prints the flags of one command.

docs.title: Flag syntax
docs.text:
Fire accepts several spellings. All of these work:

vexy-stax render scene.json --view compact
vexy-stax render scene.json --view=compact
vexy-stax dir2scene assets --floor_color '#000000'
vexy-stax dir2scene assets --floor-color '#000000'

Boolean flags need care:

To set Write Not True --reverse or --reverse=True False --nocaptions or --captions=False --captions false or --captions=false (Fire reads lowercase false as a non-empty string, which counts as true)

docs.title: dir2scene
docs.text:
Generate a scene JSON from a folder of images.

vexy-stax dir2scene DIRECTORY [FLAGS]

DIRECTORY must contain at least one .png, .jpg, .jpeg or .webp file (the extension check ignores case). Files are sorted in natural order and become slides back to front. The command prints the absolute path of the scene it wrote.

Flag Default Meaning --out scene.json Output path. If it is an existing directory, scene.json is written inside it. --view expanded Value for the scene's view field. --width first image's width size.width. --height first image's height size.height. --gap int(width × 0.38) camera.gap in points. --distance 100% camera.distance. --angle 60.0 camera.angle. --elevation 0.0 camera.elevation. --fov 39.6 camera.fov. --background #ffffff background. --floor_color #f2f2f2 floor.color. --floor_opacity 1.0 floor.opacity. --floor_reflectivity 0.5 floor.reflectivity. --transition_kind none Adds a transition block of this kind. Without it, the scene has no transition. --transition_duration 3.0 transition.duration. --transition_wait 1.0 transition.wait. --transition_fps 30 transition.fps. --transition_easing easeInOutCubic transition.easing. --reverse False Reverse the file order (use it when the folder is sorted front to back). --captions True Generate a caption per slide from its file name. --nocaptions turns this off. --juicy False Value for the scene's juicy field.

Slide paths are written relative to the output file. Each generated caption uses show_in: "expanded".

How captions are named. The prefix shared by all file names is removed, then leading and trailing digits, spaces, - and _, then - and _ become spaces and the result is title-cased. An empty result becomes Slide. In testdata/airbl-lores/ the shared prefix is airbl-0, so airbl-020-source.png becomes Source.

Warning

The generated scene contains "gap": null for every slide. An explicit null gap means minimal spacing, so the expanded view collapses. Remove the keys, for example with jq 'del(.slides[].gap)'. See Troubleshooting.

Examples:

# Scene with a round-trip transition
vexy-stax dir2scene assets --out scene.json \
  --transition_kind expand_collapse --transition_easing linear

# 4K canvas, 45° camera, no captions
vexy-stax dir2scene assets --out scene.json \
  --width 3840 --height 2160 --angle 45 --nocaptions

docs.title: render
docs.text:
Render one still.

vexy-stax render SCENE [--view expanded|compact] [--engine NAME] [--out PATH]
Flag Default Meaning --view expanded View to render. The scene's own view field is not used. --engine pygfx pygfx, blender or playwright. --out out.png Output PNG.

On success it prints Wrote OUT (engine: NAME).

vexy-stax render scene.json --view expanded --out beauty.png
vexy-stax render scene.json --view compact --engine blender --out stack.png

docs.title: video
docs.text:
Render the scene's transition to a video file. The scene must contain a transition block.

vexy-stax video SCENE [FLAGS]
Flag Default Meaning --engine blender blender, pygfx or playwright. --out out.mp4 Output video. --width scene video.width Overrides the video width for this render. --height scene video.height Overrides the video height. --fps scene video.fps Overrides the frame rate. --frames scene video.frames Overrides the transition frames per leg. --first_hold scene video.first_hold (10) Copies of the first frame at the start. --last_hold scene video.last_hold (10) Copies of the last frame at the end.

The overrides apply to this render only; the scene file is not changed.

vexy-stax video scene.json --out morph.mp4
vexy-stax video scene.json --engine pygfx --fps 24 --first_hold 0 --last_hold 0 --out preview.mp4

docs.title: overlay
docs.text:
Composite the slides into one flat PNG with Pillow.

vexy-stax overlay SCENE [--out flat.png]

The canvas is as wide as the widest image and as tall as the tallest. Each image is centred horizontally and aligned to the bottom, and the images are alpha-composited from slide 0 upward. No engine is involved, so this works without a GPU, Blender or a browser.

docs.title: engines
docs.text:
vexy-stax engines

Prints Available engines: followed by the engines whose dependency probe succeeds, for example blender, playwright, pygfx. See Installation for what each probe checks.

docs.title: Engine defaults and errors
docs.text:
Command Default engine render pygfx video blender
  • An unknown engine name prints Unknown engine 'NAME'. Registered: blender, playwright, pygfx and writes nothing.
  • An engine that raises NotImplementedError prints Engine 'NAME' not ready: with the reason.
  • Other errors, such as a missing transition or a missing ffmpeg, end with a Python traceback that names the cause.

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text:
Variable Effect VEXY_STAX_TURBO=1 The Blender engine renders with Eevee and 8 samples instead of Cycles with 16 samples. Use it for fast previews. 
VEXY_STAX_TURBO=1 vexy-stax render scene.json --engine blender --out preview.png

docs.title: Scene
docs.text: A scene is an ordered list of slides plus settings for the camera, the floor, plate borders, captions, the transition and video output. It lives in one JSON document that vexy-stax-py and vexy-stax-js both read. See Scene format.

docs.title: Slides and plates
docs.text:
Each slide is one image, drawn as a flat upright plate in 3D space. A plate's width and height in world units ("points") equal the pixel size of its image.

Slides are ordered back to front: index 0 is the farthest plate, the last slide is the closest. In the sample deck testdata/airbl-lores/, airbl-010-back.png is slide 0 and airbl-090-ui.png is the frontmost.

docs.title: The deck
docs.text:
The deck is the stack of plates along the Z axis:

  • the frontmost plate sits at Z = 0,
  • each plate behind it sits further along -Z, separated by its gap,
  • slide 0 sits at Z = -stack_depth, where stack_depth is the sum of the gaps between adjacent plates.

docs.title: Coordinate system
docs.text:
vexy-stax uses a right-handed, Y-up frame, the same one three.js uses. The Blender render script, the pygfx engine and the JS stage all build their scenes in it, so camera poses can be exchanged between renderers.

Axis Meaning X Plate width. Plates are centred on X = 0. Y Up. The floor line is Y = -height/2. Z Depth. The front plate is at Z = 0; +Z points toward the viewer.

The camera framing is computed from scene.size, so all engines frame the deck the same way even if individual images differ in size.

docs.title: Expanded
docs.text:
• The camera orbits around the deck centre by camera.angle (azimuth) and camera.elevation.
  • Plates are spaced by their gaps (camera.gap, or a per-slide gap).
  • Captions with show_in: "expanded" are visible.
  • The framing is solved automatically: the deck is centred horizontally, the left and right margins each equal the projected spacing between adjacent plates, and the deck never crops at the top or bottom.

docs.title: Compact
docs.text:
• The camera sits head-on on the +Z axis, aimed at the deck centre.
  • Every gap collapses to MIN_GAP = 3.0 points, just enough to keep plates from z-fighting.
  • The frontmost slide plate is fitted to the frame according to camera.distance (for example "100%").
  • Captions with show_in: "expanded" are hidden.

docs.title: Transitions
docs.text:
A transition animates between the two views. It is made of one or two legs:

kind Legs expand compact → expanded collapse expanded → compact expand_collapse compact → expanded, then expanded → compact collapse_expand expanded → compact, then compact → expanded

Each leg lasts duration seconds. After each leg the view holds still for wait seconds. During a leg, a morph factor t runs from 0 (compact) to 1 (expanded), or back, shaped by the easing curve. At each frame vexy-stax interpolates:

  1. the camera position, target, field of view and near plane (linear interpolation between the compact and expanded poses),
  2. every gap, from MIN_GAP to its expanded value,
  3. every slide's opacity, from its compact to its expanded value,
  4. every caption's opacity, with the staggered fade described in Captions.

Video output also holds the first and last frame for a number of frames (10 each by default), so a clip opens and closes on a still image.

docs.title: Easing
docs.text:
Four named curves are available. All interpolation in a leg uses the same curve.

Name Shape linear t easeInCubic t³: slow start, fast finish easeOutCubic 1 − (1 − t)³: fast start, slow finish easeInOutCubic 4t³ below 0.5, 1 − (−2t + 2)³ / 2 above: the default

easeInOutCubic concentrates motion in the middle of the leg. Use linear for constant-speed motion.

docs.title: Opacity
docs.text: A slide's opacity is either one number (0.8, used in both views) or a per-view object such as { "expanded": 1.0, "compact": 0.4 }. The per-view form is interpolated with the same easing as the camera. "compact": 0 hides a slide in the compact view while keeping it in the expanded view. Values are clamped to [0, 1].

docs.title: The floor
docs.text:
The floor is a horizontal plane at the bottom of the deck. It has two parts:

  • a pane, tinted with floor.color at floor.opacity,
  • a blurred reflection of the plates, scaled by floor.reflectivity. The blur radius is REFLECTION_BLUR_FRAC = 0.02 of the plate height, so the reflection reads as soft rather than mirror-sharp.

By default the pane is invisible (opacity 0.0) and the reflection is faint (reflectivity 0.1). Raise opacity for a visible floor.

docs.title: Captions and the stacked layout
docs.text:
A caption is a text label for one slide, drawn as a small opaque plate with the text on it. With captions on (captions: true, the default):

  • each caption plate stands on the floor, at its slide's depth, left-aligned with the slide plate;
  • each slide plate is lifted by one caption-plate height so it sits on top of its caption plate.

With captions: false no caption plates are drawn and the slides stand directly on the floor. See Captions for sizes, colours and fade timing.

docs.title: Plate borders
docs.text: edge.width draws a frame around every slide plate and caption plate. It is a fraction of the scene height and is 0 (off) by default. edge.color sets the border colour and is also the default fill and border colour of caption plates.

docs.title: Engines
docs.text:
vexy-stax-py has three render engines. Each implements the Engine protocol from vexy_stax.engines.base:

class Engine(Protocol):
    name: str

    def render_image(self, scene: Scene, view: View, out: Path) -> None: ...

    def render_video(self, scene: Scene, out: Path) -> None: ...

No engine computes its own camera. Every engine takes the camera pose, gaps, plate opacities and caption opacities from vexy_stax.geometry, as a single pose for stills or as the frame_plan() list for video. The engines differ only in how they draw.

docs.title: Comparison
docs.text:
pygfx blender playwright Draws with pygfx on WGPU, off-screen Blender (Cycles, or Eevee in turbo mode) in a subprocess vexy-stax-js three.js stage in headless Chromium Default for render video — Stills supersampled ×2, Lanczos downscale full scene.size supersampled ×2, Lanczos downscale Video PNG sequence + ffmpeg PNG sequence + ffmpeg, long edge capped at 1920 px captured frames + ffmpeg Needs WGPU backend; ffmpeg for video Blender binary; ffmpeg for video Chromium for Playwright, a built sibling vexy-stax-js, ffmpeg for video

All three encode video as H.264 with -crf 18 and +faststart.

docs.title: Video parameters
docs.text:
For video, every engine reads the same helpers from vexy_stax.geometry:

  • video_dimensions(scene): (video.width or size.width, video.height or size.height),
  • video_fps(scene): video.fps, else transition.fps, else 30,
  • frame_plan(scene): the list of FrameState objects, including the held first and last frames.

The held frames are plain repeated FrameState objects, so engines need no special handling for them. A scene without a transition cannot be rendered as video; the engine raises ValueError: scene has no transition; nothing to animate (use render_image).

docs.title: pygfx
docs.text:
The default for stills. It renders off-screen through rendercanvas.offscreen, so it needs no window or display.

What it builds:

  • one textured plane per slide, sized to the image's pixel dimensions,
  • a floor plane at the bottom of the deck, drawn with floor.color and floor.opacity,
  • a faded, blurred mirror copy of each plate below the floor line for the reflection (floor.reflectivity),
  • caption plates: an opaque quad with an optional border and centred text, registered with the bundled vexy-stax.ttf unless the scene sets another font,
  • a perspective camera from compact_camera() or expanded_camera().

Plates cast no shadow on the floor.

pygfx's PerspectiveCamera.fov is not a horizontal field of view, so the engine converts the scene's horizontal fov before use. That keeps its framing equal to Blender and three.js.

For video it renders each FrameState to a PNG and assembles the sequence with ffmpeg. Missing ffmpeg raises FileNotFoundError: ffmpeg not found on PATH.

Use pygfx for quick stills, batch work and tests: it starts in seconds and needs no external program for stills.

docs.title: blender
docs.text:
The default for video. The Python side builds a job description (plates, camera, captions, frames) and runs Blender in the background with the bundled script, passing the job as JSON after --:

blender --background --python vexy_stax/engines/_blender_render.py -- '{...job JSON...}'

The script builds the scene inside Blender and renders it.

Finding Blender: blender on PATH, then /opt/homebrew/bin/blender, then /Applications/Blender.app/Contents/MacOS/Blender. If none exists it raises FileNotFoundError with an install hint.

Render settings:

Setting Default With VEXY_STAX_TURBO=1 Renderer Cycles Eevee Samples 16 8 Denoiser OpenImageDenoise — Cycles max_bounces 4 — Cycles transparent_max_bounces max(64, 4 × number of plates) —

The high transparent-bounce limit keeps the dense head-on stack of the compact view from rendering black.

For video, the engine keys every frame from frame_plan(), renders a PNG sequence and assembles it with ffmpeg. It caps the video's long edge at 1920 pixels, keeping the aspect ratio: a 3840 × 2480 scene renders a 1920 × 1240 video. Stills use the full scene.size.

Use Blender for final output, especially decks with many transparent layers.

docs.title: playwright
docs.text:
The Playwright engine reuses the browser renderer instead of drawing on its own:

  1. It serves the directory that contains both checkouts over a local HTTP server, so textures load without file:// restrictions.
  2. It opens a generated harness page in headless Chromium. The page loads vexy-stax-js/dist/vexy-stax.element.js and mounts the scene in a <vexy-stax> element. Slide paths are rewritten to http:// URLs under the served root.
  3. For a still, it screenshots the WebGL canvas.
  4. For video, it computes frame_plan() in Python, sends each FrameState to the page's stage.applyFrameState, captures the canvas, and assembles the frames with ffmpeg.

The engine locates the bundle at ../vexy-stax-js/dist/vexy-stax.element.js relative to the vexy-stax-py checkout. If it is missing, rendering fails with FileNotFoundError and the build command. It therefore works from a development checkout of both repositories, not from a wheel installed on its own.

Use it to compare the Python output with what the browser component renders.

docs.title: Registry
docs.text:
Engines register themselves when vexy_stax.engines first needs them.

from pathlib import Path

from vexy_stax.engines import all_engines, available_engines, get_engine, is_available
from vexy_stax.scene import load_scene

print(all_engines())          # ['blender', 'playwright', 'pygfx']
print(available_engines())    # only those whose probe succeeds
print(is_available("blender"))

engine = get_engine("pygfx")  # KeyError for an unknown name
engine.render_image(load_scene("scene.json"), "expanded", Path("beauty.png"))

The availability probes are cheap: shutil.which("blender") for Blender, and importlib.util.find_spec(...) for pygfx and playwright.

docs.title: Adding an engine
docs.text:
1. Create src/vexy_stax/engines/myengine.py with a class that has name = "myengine", render_image() and render_video(). Raise NotImplementedError for anything not supported yet; the CLI reports it as "not ready".
  2. Take every camera pose and per-frame value from vexy_stax.geometry; don't recompute them.
  3. Call register(MyEngine()) at module level.
  4. Add an availability probe for "myengine" to _PROBES in engines/base.py.
  5. Import the module in _ensure_loaded() in engines/base.py.
  6. Add tests with a pytest marker that skips when the engine is unavailable, like the existing blender, pygfx and playwright markers in pyproject.toml.

docs.title: Geometry
docs.text:
All view math lives in src/vexy_stax/geometry.py. The module is pure: it uses math and the standard library, holds no rendering code, and returns plain values and frozen dataclasses. All three Python engines use it, and vexy-stax-js mirrors it in geometry.js. The repository's SPEC.md (section 3) is the normative description.

The examples on this page use a default scene with three captioned slides and an expand transition: size 1920 × 1080, camera.gap 1920, angle 60, elevation 0, fov 39.6, distance "100%".

docs.title: Data types
docs.text:
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class CameraPose:
    position: tuple[float, float, float]
    target: tuple[float, float, float]
    fov: float   # degrees, horizontal
    near: float  # near clipping plane

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class FrameState:
    camera: CameraPose
    gaps: list[float]               # per-slide gap
    opacities: list[float]          # per-slide plate opacity
    caption_opacities: list[float]  # per-slide caption opacity

docs.title: Gaps and stack depth
docs.text:
plate_gaps(scene) returns one gap per slide: the slide's own gap, or camera.gap when the slide omits the key, with 0 replaced by MIN_GAP (3.0).

stack_depth(scene, view) is the sum of the gaps between adjacent plates:

  • "compact": (N − 1) × MIN_GAP. Three slides give 6.0.
  • "expanded": the sum of the per-slide gaps. Three slides with gap 1920 give 3840.0.

The front plate sits at Z = 0, slide 0 at Z = −stack_depth, and the deck centre at Z = −stack_depth / 2.

docs.title: Slide lift
docs.text: With captions on, slide_lift(scene) returns one caption-plate height (144 points in the example), and every slide plate centre moves up by that amount so the slide sits on its caption plate. With captions: false the lift is 0.

docs.title: Compact camera
docs.text:
compact_camera(scene, viewport_aspect=None) puts the camera on the +Z axis, aimed at the centre of the frontmost slide plate:

target   = (0, lift, −stack_depth/2)
position = target + (0, 0, distance)
near     = max(1.0, distance × 0.005)

For a percentage distance such as "100%", the frontmost slide plate (scene.size) is fitted so the limiting axis fills P % of the frame:

hfov  = camera.fov
vfov  = 2 · atan(tan(hfov/2) / aspect)
d_w   = width  / (2 · tan(hfov/2) · P/100)
d_h   = height / (2 · tan(vfov/2) · P/100)
distance = max(d_w, d_h) + stack_depth/2

aspect is viewport_aspect when given, otherwise width / height. A numeric distance is used as is.

In the example: target = (0, 144, −3), position ≈ (0, 144, 2666.5), near ≈ 13.3.

docs.title: Expanded camera
docs.text:
expanded_camera(scene, viewport_aspect=None) orbits the camera around the deck centre. The direction from target to camera is

to_cam = normalize(−sin(az)·cos(el),  sin(el),  cos(az)·cos(el))

with az = angle and el = elevation in radians. az = 0 is head-on; positive angles swing toward −X.

The distance and a horizontal pan are then solved so that, in the projected image:

  1. the deck is centred: the left margin equals the right margin,
  2. each margin equals the mean projected horizontal distance between adjacent plate centres,
  3. the deck's vertical extent fits within V_FILL = 0.98 of the frame height, so nothing crops at the top or bottom. The bounds include the lifted slides and, with captions on, the caption row on the floor.

The solve uses bisection. Re-centring the pan runs 64 iterations; the margin-equals-gap distance and the vertical-fit distance run 80 iterations each, and the camera uses the larger of the two distances. The initial bracket comes from a bounding-box fit at FILL = 0.85. Bisection is deterministic, so Python and JavaScript converge to the same pose.

In the example the expanded camera lands at position ≈ (−9168.5, 0, 3403.5), looking at target ≈ (13.0, 0, −1897.5).

docs.title: Transition frames
docs.text:
frame_plan(scene, first_hold=None, last_hold=None) returns the list of FrameState objects for the scene's transition, or [] without one.

For each leg, for frame i of leg_frames:

p = i / leg_frames          # 0 ≤ p < 1
t = start + (end − start) · ease(easing, p)

t is the morph factor (0 = compact, 1 = expanded). The frame state at t is

gaps[i]      = MIN_GAP + (expanded_gap[i] − MIN_GAP) · t
opacities[i] = compact_opacity + (expanded_opacity − compact_opacity) · t
camera       = linear interpolation of position, target, fov and near
caption_opacities = caption_opacities(scene, t)

After each leg, round(wait × fps) copies of the end state are appended. Finally the whole list is bookended with first_hold copies of the first state and last_hold copies of the last; both default to the scene's video.first_hold and video.last_hold.

Related helpers:

Function Returns video_fps(scene) video.fps, else transition.fps, else 30 video_dimensions(scene) (video.width or size.width, video.height or size.height) transition_frames(scene) video.frames, else round(duration × video_fps); 0 without a transition

For the example expand transition: transition_frames is 90, the wait adds 30, and the holds add 20, so len(frame_plan(scene)) == 140.

docs.title: Easing
docs.text: ease(name, t) clamps t to [0, 1] and evaluates linear, easeInCubic, easeOutCubic or easeInOutCubic. Any other name raises ValueError. For example ease("easeOutCubic", 0.8) returns 0.992.

docs.title: Opacity
docs.text: interpolate_opacity(slide, t_expanded) interpolates between the slide's compact and expanded opacity and clamps the result to [0, 1].

docs.title: Constants
docs.text: Constant Value Use MIN_GAP 3.0 Compact spacing; replaces a zero gap. FILL 0.85 Bracket for the expanded distance solve. V_FILL 0.98 Maximum vertical fraction of the frame the expanded deck may fill. REFLECTION_BLUR_FRAC 0.02 Reflection blur radius as a fraction of the plate height. CAPTION_FADE_WINDOW 0.9 Default caption_fade.window. CAPTION_STAGGER 0.3 Default caption_fade.stagger. CAPTION_PLATE_HEIGHT_FRAC 0.1 × 4/3 ≈ 0.1333 Default caption-plate height as a fraction of the scene height. CAPTION_FONT_FRAC_OF_PLATE 0.75 Text size as a fraction of the caption-plate height. CAPTION_PLATE_PAD_EM 0.75 Horizontal padding on each side of the caption text, in em. CAPTION_BASELINE_EM 1.0 Text baseline height above the floor, in em. CAPTION_GAP_EM 0.0 Horizontal offset of the caption anchor, in em.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Python 3.12 or newer (requires-python = ">=3.12").
  • uv (recommended) or pip.

Installing the package also installs its Python dependencies: fire, rich, pillow, numpy, pydantic (v2), opencv-python-headless, pygfx, pylinalg and playwright. Some engines need more than a Python package; see Engine prerequisites.

docs.title: Install from PyPI
docs.text:
The package is published as vexy-stax:

pip install vexy-stax

or, inside a uv project:

uv add vexy-stax

Both install the vexy-stax command. You can also run the CLI as a module:

python -m vexy_stax engines

docs.title: Install from a checkout
docs.text:
Use this when you want to change the code or run the tests.

  1. Clone the repository:

    git clone https://github.com/vexyart/vexy-stax-py.git
cd vexy-stax-py

  2. Create the virtual environment and install the package with its development dependencies:

    uv venv --python 3.12
uv sync

  3. Run the CLI from the environment:

    uv run vexy-stax engines

The version is derived from the git tags by hatch-vcs, so a checkout needs its git history (not a bare source export) to report a proper version.

docs.title: Verify the install
docs.text:
vexy-stax engines

The command prints the engines whose dependencies are present, in registration order, for example:

Available engines: blender, playwright, pygfx

The check is cheap and does not import the engines:

Engine Listed when blender a blender binary is on PATH pygfx the pygfx Python package is importable playwright the playwright Python package is importable

Because pygfx and playwright are package dependencies, both are normally listed. Being listed does not guarantee the engine can render; the next section lists what each one still needs.

docs.title: pygfx
docs.text:
pygfx renders off-screen through WGPU and needs a working WGPU backend (Metal on macOS, Vulkan or DirectX elsewhere). Stills need nothing else.

For video, pygfx writes a PNG sequence and assembles it with ffmpeg, which must be on PATH:

brew install ffmpeg        # macOS
sudo apt install ffmpeg    # Debian/Ubuntu

Without it the video command fails with ffmpeg not found on PATH.

docs.title: Blender
docs.text:
vexy-stax runs Blender as a separate process. Install Blender and make the blender binary reachable. The engine looks for it in this order:

  1. blender on PATH
  2. /opt/homebrew/bin/blender
  3. /Applications/Blender.app/Contents/MacOS/Blender

On macOS, brew install --cask blender works. To put the app bundle's binary on PATH:

export PATH="/Applications/Blender.app/Contents/MacOS:$PATH"
blender --version

vexy-stax engines only checks PATH, so a Blender found through the fallback paths still renders but is not listed.

Blender video also assembles frames with ffmpeg.

docs.title: Playwright
docs.text:
The Playwright engine drives headless Chromium. Install the browser once:

python -m playwright install chromium

It also needs the built vexy-stax-js bundle. The engine expects a vexy-stax-js checkout next to the vexy-stax-py checkout and loads vexy-stax-js/dist/vexy-stax.element.js from it. If the bundle is missing, the engine tells you how to build it:

cd ../vexy-stax-js && npm install && npm run build

In practice this engine is meant for a development checkout of both repositories, not for a plain pip install.

Playwright video also assembles frames with ffmpeg.

docs.title: The bundled caption font
docs.text:
The wheel ships a caption font:

vexy_stax/fonts/vexy-stax.ttf   # Zalando Sans Expanded
vexy_stax/fonts/OFL.txt         # SIL Open Font License

Captions use it whenever the scene sets no font. To find it from Python:

from vexy_stax.geometry import default_font_path

print(default_font_path())  # Path to vexy-stax.ttf, or None if missing

docs.title: Run the tests
docs.text:
From a checkout:

uv run pytest -q

The default selection excludes tests marked slow. Tests marked blender, pygfx or playwright skip themselves when their engine is unavailable.

docs.title: Python API
docs.text:
Every CLI command is a thin wrapper around the package modules, so anything the CLI does you can do from Python.

Module Contents vexy_stax.scene Pydantic v2 scene model and load_scene() vexy_stax.geometry Camera poses, gaps, opacities, caption layout, frame plans vexy_stax.engines Engine protocol and registry vexy_stax.images Pillow image reading and flat compositing vexy_stax.juicy Per-channel colour matching between renders vexy_stax.showcase The showcase runner behind example.py vexy_stax.cli The Stax Fire CLI and main()

vexy_stax.__version__ holds the installed version.

docs.title: Render a scene
docs.text:
from pathlib import Path

from vexy_stax.engines import available_engines, get_engine
from vexy_stax.scene import load_scene

scene = load_scene("scene.json")
print("Available:", available_engines())

pygfx = get_engine("pygfx")
pygfx.render_image(scene, "expanded", Path("beauty.png"))
pygfx.render_image(scene, "compact", Path("stack.png"))

get_engine("blender").render_video(scene, Path("morph.mp4"))

docs.title: load_scene(path)
docs.text:
Reads a JSON file, validates it against the Scene model and resolves every slide src against the scene file's directory (absolute paths and data: URIs are kept). Invalid input raises pydantic.ValidationError.

from vexy_stax.scene import load_scene

scene = load_scene("scene.json")
scene.slides[0].src   # absolute path string
scene.camera.gap      # float

docs.title: Model classes
docs.text:
from vexy_stax.scene import (
    Scene, Slide, Caption, CaptionStyle, CaptionFade,
    Camera, Transition, Video, Floor, Edge, Size, OpacityPerView,
    View, TransitionKind, ShowIn, Easing,
)

Every model sets extra="forbid". The type aliases are:

Alias Values View "expanded", "compact" TransitionKind "expand", "collapse", "expand_collapse", "collapse_expand" ShowIn "expanded", "compact", "both", "none" Easing "linear", "easeInOutCubic", "easeOutCubic", "easeInCubic"

Slide.resolved_opacity(view) returns the slide's opacity in one view, whether opacity is a number or an OpacityPerView.

docs.title: Build a scene in code
docs.text:
from vexy_stax.scene import Camera, Caption, Scene, Size, Slide, Transition

scene = Scene(
    size=Size(width=1920, height=1080),
    camera=Camera(gap=1200, angle=50),
    transition=Transition(kind="expand_collapse", easing="linear"),
    slides=[
        Slide(src="/abs/layer-0.png", caption=Caption(text="Background")),
        Slide(src="/abs/layer-1.png", caption=Caption(text="Content")),
        Slide(src="/abs/layer-2.png", opacity={"expanded": 1.0, "compact": 0.0}),
    ],
)

Paths in a scene built this way are not resolved; use absolute paths. Leave gap unset on a slide to inherit camera.gap; gap=0 gives MIN_GAP.

docs.title: Save a scene
docs.text:
from pathlib import Path

Path("scene.json").write_text(scene.model_dump_json(by_alias=True, indent=2, exclude_none=True))

by_alias=True writes the $schema key under its JSON name. exclude_none=True leaves out unset optional fields, including per-slide gap: null, which would otherwise read back as "minimal gap".

docs.title: vexy_stax.geometry
docs.text:
All functions take a Scene and return plain values. See Geometry for the formulas.

from vexy_stax import geometry as g

g.compact_camera(scene)            # CameraPose
g.expanded_camera(scene)           # CameraPose
g.compact_camera(scene, viewport_aspect=2.0)

g.plate_gaps(scene)                # list[float]
g.stack_depth(scene, "expanded")   # float
g.slide_lift(scene)                # float

g.frame_plan(scene)                # list[FrameState]
g.frame_plan(scene, first_hold=0, last_hold=0)
g.transition_frames(scene)         # frames per leg
g.video_fps(scene)                 # int
g.video_dimensions(scene)          # (width, height)

g.ease("easeInOutCubic", 0.5)      # 0.5
g.interpolate_opacity(scene.slides[0], 0.5)
g.caption_opacities(scene, 0.75)   # list[float]

g.caption_size(scene)              # 1 em in points
g.caption_plate_height(scene)
g.caption_plate_center_y(scene)
g.caption_baseline_y(scene)
g.caption_anchor_x(scene)
g.caption_fill_color(scene)        # hex string
g.caption_border_color(scene)      # hex string
g.plate_edge_width(scene)          # border thickness in points

g.default_font_path()              # Path to vexy-stax.ttf, or None

docs.title: vexy_stax.engines
docs.text:
from vexy_stax.engines import Engine, all_engines, available_engines, get_engine, is_available, register
Function Returns all_engines() every registered name: ['blender', 'playwright', 'pygfx'] available_engines() registered names whose dependency probe succeeds is_available(name) True if the probe for name succeeds get_engine(name) the engine instance; KeyError for an unknown name register(engine) registers an engine instance under engine.name

render_image(scene, view, out) writes a PNG; render_video(scene, out) writes an MP4 and raises ValueError when the scene has no transition. See Engines.

docs.title: vexy_stax.images
docs.text:
from vexy_stax.images import overlay_images, read_images

infos = read_images(["/abs/layer-0.png", "/abs/layer-1.png"])
# [{'path': ..., 'width': ..., 'height': ...}, ...]
overlay_images(infos, "flat.png")

overlay_images builds a canvas as large as the widest and tallest image, centres each image horizontally, aligns it to the bottom, and alpha-composites from index 0 (back) to the last (front). It is what vexy-stax overlay runs.

docs.title: vexy_stax.juicy
docs.text:
Per-channel linear colour correction. It compares a flat Pillow overlay with a 3D stack render and corrects the render toward the overlay's colours.

from vexy_stax.juicy import apply_still, apply_video, compute_corrections

corrections = compute_corrections("flat.png", "stack.png")  # (scale, offset) per channel, B, G, R order
apply_still("beauty.png", corrections)                      # rewrites the PNG in place
apply_video("morph.mp4", corrections)                       # re-encodes the video with ffmpeg

compute_corrections matches the mean and standard deviation of each channel inside the overlay's opaque area. apply_still also pushes near-white pixels to pure white.

The scene's juicy flag records the intent, but the render and video commands don't call these functions; call them yourself.

docs.title: vexy_stax.showcase
docs.text: run_showcase(...) renders a compact still, an expanded still and a short transition video of testdata/airbl.scene.json with each available engine into outputs/<engine>/, and checks that each still is not blank (pixel standard deviation above STD_GATE = 20.0). example.py in the repository root calls it. It is a development tool and expects a repository checkout.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text: This walk-through takes a folder of layered PNGs to an expanded still, a compact still and a transition video. It uses the low-resolution sample deck that ships in the repository, testdata/airbl-lores/: nine PNGs, 1247 × 806 pixels, named airbl-010-back.png through airbl-090-ui.png.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• vexy-stax installed (see Installation).
  • For the video step: ffmpeg on PATH, and either Blender (the default video engine) or the pygfx engine.

docs.title: 1. Generate a scene file
docs.text:
vexy-stax dir2scene testdata/airbl-lores --out scene.json --transition_kind expand

dir2scene does the following:

  1. Collects the .png, .jpg, .jpeg and .webp files in the folder.
  2. Sorts them in natural order, so 2.png comes before 10.png. The first file becomes slide 0, the farthest plate.
  3. Reads the first image's size and uses it as the scene size, here 1247 × 806.
  4. Sets the expanded plate spacing camera.gap to 38 % of the width, rounded down: int(1247 × 0.38) = 473.
  5. Builds a caption from each file name. It strips the prefix shared by all names (airbl-0), strips leading and trailing digits and separators, replaces - and _ with spaces, and title-cases the rest. airbl-020-source.png becomes Source; airbl-090-ui.png becomes Ui.
  6. Because --transition_kind expand is set, adds a transition block (duration 3.0 s, wait 1.0 s, 30 fps, easeInOutCubic).
  7. Writes the scene and prints its absolute path. Slide paths are written relative to the scene file.

Remove the explicit gap: null entries

dir2scene writes "gap": null into every slide. In the scene format an explicit null gap means "minimal gap", so every plate collapses to 3 points in the expanded view too. Delete the per-slide gap keys so the slides inherit camera.gap, for example with jq:

jq 'del(.slides[].gap)' scene.json > scene.tmp && mv scene.tmp scene.json

docs.title: 2. Render the expanded view
docs.text:
vexy-stax render scene.json --view expanded --out beauty.png

With no --engine, stills use pygfx. The command prints Wrote beauty.png (engine: pygfx). The camera is placed by an automatic framing solve: the deck is centred, and the margins on both sides equal the projected spacing between adjacent plates.

docs.title: 3. Render the compact view
docs.text:
vexy-stax render scene.json --view compact --out stack.png

The camera now looks straight down the +Z axis, the plates sit 3 points apart, and the frontmost plate fills the frame (camera.distance is "100%"). Captions with show_in: "expanded" (the dir2scene default) are hidden.

docs.title: 4. Render the transition video
docs.text:
vexy-stax video scene.json --out morph.mp4

With no --engine, video uses blender. For a faster preview use --engine pygfx.

The frame count comes from the scene. For this expand transition at 30 fps:

Part Frames Held first frame (video.first_hold) 10 Transition leg (round(3.0 × 30)) 90 Hold at the end of the leg (round(1.0 × 30)) 30 Held last frame (video.last_hold) 10 Total 140

You can override the video settings without editing the scene:

vexy-stax video scene.json --engine pygfx --fps 24 --first_hold 0 --last_hold 0 --out morph.mp4

docs.title: 5. Make a flat preview
docs.text:
vexy-stax overlay scene.json --out flat.png

This composites the slides with Pillow, bottom-aligned and horizontally centred, without any 3D engine. It is a quick way to check that the layers line up.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Adjust the camera, floor or captions: see the Scene reference.
  • Pick an engine for the job: see Engines.
  • Script the same steps in Python: see Python API.

docs.title: One format, two readers
docs.text:
A scene is one JSON document. Both packages read it:

  • vexy-stax-py parses it into the Pydantic v2 model in vexy_stax.scene.
  • vexy-stax-js parses it with its own scene.js.

The JSON Schema is schema/vexy-stax-scene.schema.json (draft 2020-12, $id https://vexy.art/schema/vexy-stax-scene.schema.json). Both readers reject unknown fields: every Pydantic model sets extra="forbid", and the schema sets additionalProperties: false. A typo in a field name fails loudly when the scene is loaded instead of being silently ignored.

docs.title: Minimal scene
docs.text:
{
  "version": 1,
  "slides": [
    { "src": "layer-0-background.png" },
    { "src": "layer-1-content.png" },
    { "src": "layer-2-ui.png" }
  ]
}

The schema requires version (always 1) and slides (at least one entry with a src). Every other field has a default.

docs.title: Annotated scene
docs.text:
The comments below are for explanation only; JSON itself does not allow comments.

{
  "$schema": "https://vexy.art/schema/vexy-stax-scene.schema.json", // optional, ignored
  "version": 1,
  "view": "expanded",                       // initial view: expanded | compact
  "size": { "width": 1920, "height": 1080 },// output size in pixels (= points)

  "camera": {
    "gap": 1920,          // points between adjacent plates in the expanded view
    "distance": "100%",   // absolute points, or "P%" fit of the frontmost plate
    "angle": 60,          // expanded camera azimuth, degrees
    "elevation": 0,       // expanded camera elevation, degrees
    "fov": 39.6           // horizontal field of view, degrees
  },

  "transition": {         // omit for still-only scenes
    "kind": "expand_collapse",
    "duration": 3.0,      // seconds per leg
    "wait": 1.0,          // hold after each leg, seconds
    "fps": 30,
    "easing": "easeInOutCubic"
  },

  "video": {              // video output settings; all optional
    "width": null, "height": null, "fps": null, "frames": null,
    "first_hold": 10, "last_hold": 10
  },

  "floor": { "color": "#ffffff", "opacity": 0.0, "reflectivity": 0.1 },
  "edge":  { "width": 0.0, "color": "#f2f2f2" },
  "background": "#ffffff",
  "juicy": false,
  "captions": true,       // global caption switch

  "caption_defaults": {   // default caption style
    "size": null, "color": null, "font": null,
    "fill_color": null, "border_color": null
  },
  "caption_fade": { "window": 0.9, "stagger": 0.3, "stagger_frames": null },

  "slides": [             // back to front; index 0 is the farthest plate
    {
      "src": "layer-0-background.png",
      "caption": { "text": "Background" }
    },
    {
      "src": "layer-1-content.png",
      "opacity": { "expanded": 1.0, "compact": 0.6 },
      "caption": { "text": "Content", "show_in": "expanded" }
    },
    {
      "src": "layer-2-ui.png",
      "gap": 400,
      "caption": { "text": "UI", "style": { "color": "#0066cc" } }
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Top-level fields
docs.text:
Field Type Default Meaning version integer 1 Format version. Must be 1. slides array — Slides, back to front. At least one. view string "expanded" Initial view. size object 1920 × 1080 Output size in pixels. camera object see reference Camera and expanded spacing. transition object or null null The animation. Required for video. video object see reference Video size, frame rate and held frames. floor object invisible pane, faint reflection Floor appearance. edge object width 0 Plate borders. background string "#ffffff" Background colour. juicy boolean false Python-only colour-matching flag. captions boolean true Draw caption plates at all. caption_defaults object or null null Default caption style. caption_fade object or null null Caption fade timing. $schema string — Optional schema pointer; accepted and ignored.

Every field is described in the Scene reference.

docs.title: How slide paths are resolved
docs.text:
load_scene() resolves each slide's src against the directory of the scene file and stores the absolute path. Absolute paths stay as they are. data: URIs are left untouched.

For a scene at /work/deck/scene.json:

src in the file After loading layers/a.png /work/deck/layers/a.png ../shared/b.png /work/shared/b.png /abs/c.png /abs/c.png data:image/png;base64,... unchanged

docs.title: Generating a scene
docs.text: vexy-stax dir2scene DIRECTORY writes a complete scene from a folder of images. See Quick start for a worked example and CLI for every flag. Note the per-slide "gap": null issue described there.

docs.title: Validating a scene
docs.text:
Load it with the Python model. Invalid input raises pydantic.ValidationError, which names the offending field:

from vexy_stax.scene import load_scene

scene = load_scene("scene.json")

Any JSON Schema validator also works against schema/vexy-stax-scene.schema.json.

docs.title: Scene reference
docs.text: Field-by-field reference for scene format version 1. The defaults below are the defaults of the Pydantic model in src/vexy_stax/scene.py, which mirrors schema/vexy-stax-scene.schema.json.

docs.title: version
docs.text: Integer, must be 1. The schema requires it; the Python model fills in 1 when it is missing.

docs.title: view
docs.text: "expanded" (default) or "compact". The initial view of the scene. The CLI render command takes its view from --view, not from this field.

docs.title: size
docs.text:
Field Type Default Meaning width integer ≥ 1 1920 Output width in pixels. height integer ≥ 1 1080 Output height in pixels.

The size is also the nominal plate size used for camera framing, so Python and JS frame identically.

docs.title: camera
docs.text:
Field Type Default Meaning gap number ≥ 0 1920 Points between adjacent plates in the expanded view. 0 resolves to MIN_GAP (3.0). distance number or string "100%" Compact-view camera distance. See below. angle number 60 Expanded-camera azimuth in degrees. 0 is head-on; positive values swing the camera toward -X. elevation number 0 Expanded-camera elevation in degrees above the horizon. fov number, 0 < fov < 180 39.6 Horizontal field of view in degrees.

distance takes two forms:

  • A percentage string such as "100%" or "90%". The frontmost slide plate is fitted so that the limiting axis fills that percentage of the frame; the other axis only gains padding, never crops. "90%" leaves 10 % padding on the limiting axis.
  • A number or numeric string such as 2000 or "2000": an absolute distance in points.

The expanded camera ignores distance; its distance comes from the framing solve (see Geometry).

docs.title: transition
docs.text:
Optional. Omit it for still-only scenes. Video rendering requires it.

Field Type Default Meaning kind string — (required) expand, collapse, expand_collapse or collapse_expand. duration number > 0 3.0 Seconds per leg. wait number ≥ 0 1.0 Seconds to hold at the end of each leg. fps integer ≥ 1 30 Frame rate, unless video.fps overrides it. easing string "easeInOutCubic" linear, easeInOutCubic, easeOutCubic or easeInCubic.

docs.title: video
docs.text:
Output settings for video rendering. transition defines the animation; video defines the output.

Field Type Default Meaning width integer ≥ 1 or null null → size.width Video width. height integer ≥ 1 or null null → size.height Video height. fps integer ≥ 1 or null null → transition.fps, else 30 Frame rate. Overrides transition.fps when set. frames integer ≥ 1 or null null → round(duration × fps) Transition frames per leg. first_hold integer ≥ 0 10 Copies of the first frame added at the start. last_hold integer ≥ 0 10 Copies of the last frame added at the end.

Total frame count:

total = first_hold + legs × (frames + round(wait × fps)) + last_hold

For expand_collapse with duration 3.0, wait 1.0 and 30 fps: 10 + 2 × (90 + 30) + 10 = 260 frames.

All six values can be overridden per render with the video command flags (--width, --height, --fps, --frames, --first_hold, --last_hold). The Blender engine additionally caps video at 1920 pixels on the long edge.

docs.title: floor
docs.text:
Field Type Default Meaning color string "#ffffff" Tint of the floor pane. opacity number 0–1 0.0 Opacity of the floor pane. 0 hides the pane. reflectivity number 0–1 0.1 Strength of the blurred plate reflection. 0 turns it off.

dir2scene writes different values: color #f2f2f2, opacity 1.0, reflectivity 0.5 (changeable with its --floor_* flags).

docs.title: edge
docs.text:
Field Type Default Meaning width number ≥ 0 0.0 Border thickness as a fraction of the scene height. 0 turns borders off on slide and caption plates. color string "#f2f2f2" Border colour. Also the default caption-plate fill and border colour.

For a 1080-pixel-high scene, width: 0.004 gives a border of about 4.3 points.

docs.title: background
docs.text: Background colour as a hex string. Default "#ffffff".

docs.title: juicy
docs.text: Boolean, default false. Marks a scene for per-channel colour matching between the 3D render and the flat Pillow overlay. The matching functions live in vexy_stax.juicy (see Python API); the render and video commands don't apply them. vexy-stax-js ignores this field.

docs.title: captions
docs.text: Boolean, default true. With true, caption plates are drawn and slide plates are lifted to sit on top of them. With false, no caption plates are drawn at all and slides stand on the floor.

docs.title: caption_defaults
docs.text:
Default caption style, used by every caption that doesn't override a field in its own style.

Field Type Default Meaning size number > 0 or null null Caption text size (1 em) in points. null → 10 % of the scene height, at least 8 points. color string or null null Text colour. Engines fall back to #222222. font string or null null Font. null → the bundled vexy-stax.ttf. A path to a font file works in every engine. The Blender engine replaces anything else with the bundled font; pygfx passes other family names to its font manager. fill_color string or null null Caption-plate fill. null → edge.color. border_color string or null null Caption-plate border. null → edge.color.

docs.title: caption_fade
docs.text:
Timing of the caption fade-in during a transition. When omitted, window 0.9 and stagger 0.3 apply.

Field Type Default Meaning window number, 0 < w ≤ 1 0.9 Fraction of the morph, counted back from the expanded end, during which captions fade in. stagger number, 0 ≤ s < 1 0.3 Back-to-front spread of the fade starts, as a fraction of window. stagger_frames integer ≥ 0 or null null Step between captions in transition frames. Overrides stagger when set.

See Captions for the exact formula.

docs.title: slides
docs.text:
An array of at least one slide, ordered back to front.

Field Type Default Meaning src string — (required) Image path relative to the scene file, an absolute path, or a data: URI. gap number ≥ 0 or null key omitted Expanded-view gap for this slide. See below. opacity number or object 1.0 Plate opacity: one number, or { "expanded": x, "compact": y }. caption object or null null The slide's caption.

docs.title: Per-slide gap has three states
docs.text:
In the file Effect key omitted inherits camera.gap "gap": 400 uses 400 points "gap": null or "gap": 0 uses MIN_GAP (3.0), the compact spacing

Note

dir2scene writes "gap": null for every slide, which collapses the expanded view. Remove those keys after generating a scene.

docs.title: caption
docs.text: Field Type Default Meaning text string — (required) The caption text. show_in string "expanded" expanded, compact, both or none. style object or null null Per-caption overrides; same fields as caption_defaults.

docs.title: Expanded view looks collapsed
docs.text:
Symptom. A scene made with dir2scene renders the expanded view with all plates pressed together.

Cause. dir2scene writes "gap": null into every slide. An explicit null (or 0) per-slide gap means "minimal gap" (MIN_GAP, 3 points). Only an omitted key inherits camera.gap.

Fix. Remove the per-slide gap keys:

jq 'del(.slides[].gap)' scene.json > scene.tmp && mv scene.tmp scene.json

When you write scenes from Python, save with model_dump_json(by_alias=True, exclude_none=True).

docs.title: --captions false still generates captions
docs.text: Fire reads lowercase false as a string, and any non-empty string counts as true. Use --nocaptions or --captions=False. The same applies to --reverse and --juicy.

docs.title: Unknown engine 'NAME'
docs.text: The --engine value must be pygfx, blender or playwright. The message lists the registered names. Nothing is written.

docs.title: scene has no transition; nothing to animate
docs.text: vexy-stax video needs a transition block. Add one to the scene, or regenerate it with dir2scene --transition_kind expand (or collapse, expand_collapse, collapse_expand).

docs.title: ffmpeg not found on PATH
docs.text: All three engines assemble video with ffmpeg. Install it (brew install ffmpeg, sudo apt install ffmpeg) and make sure it is on PATH. Stills don't need it.

docs.title: Blender not found
docs.text:
The Blender engine looks for blender on PATH, then /opt/homebrew/bin/blender, then /Applications/Blender.app/Contents/MacOS/Blender. Install Blender (brew install --cask blender on macOS) or add its binary to PATH.

vexy-stax engines lists Blender only when it is on PATH, even if one of the fallback locations works.

docs.title: built JS bundle not found
docs.text:
The Playwright engine needs vexy-stax-js/dist/vexy-stax.element.js in a vexy-stax-js checkout next to vexy-stax-py. Build it:

cd ../vexy-stax-js && npm install && npm run build

If Chromium is missing, install it with python -m playwright install chromium.

docs.title: Blender renders are slow
docs.text:
Cycles renders every frame of a transition, and the compact view sends rays through the whole transparent stack. Options:

  • Set VEXY_STAX_TURBO=1 to render with Eevee and 8 samples.
  • Render previews with --engine pygfx.
  • Lower the frame count: vexy-stax video scene.json --fps 24 --frames 48.

Blender video is already capped at 1920 pixels on the long edge.

docs.title: A video is longer than duration suggests
docs.text: Videos include held frames: first_hold and last_hold (10 each by default) plus round(wait × fps) frames after every leg. Set --first_hold 0 --last_hold 0, or "wait": 0 in the transition, for a clip with no holds.

docs.title: Captions are missing from the compact view
docs.text: That is the default: show_in: "expanded" captions are invisible in the compact view and fade in during the expand. Use "show_in": "both" for a caption that is always visible.

docs.title: The scene fails to load
docs.text:
load_scene() raises pydantic.ValidationError with the path of the bad field. Common causes:

  • a misspelled or unknown field (every model forbids extra fields),
  • version other than 1,
  • an empty slides array,
  • a value out of range, such as fov of 180 or a negative gap.

An image that doesn't exist fails later, when an engine or overlay reads it, with FileNotFoundError: Image not found: PATH.
